text: {"findings":[{"rule":"K2","where":"ClaimIssuer.revokeClaim / ClaimIssuer.isClaimValid / Identity.addClaim / Token.transfer (via IdentityRegistry.isVerified)","severity":"HIGH","why":"Revocation is stored by the raw signature bytes, but ECDSA signatures are malleable. ecrecover accepts the high-s form (r, n-s, v^1), which recovers the same issuer signer and is not in revokedClaims. A revoked investor can therefore re-add the claim with the malleated signature, and isVerified will pass again so the wallet can receive tokens.","steps":"1) claimIssuer.revokeClaim(keccak(claimIssuer, KYC_TOPIC), idA) marks the original sig as revoked. 2) As a1 (management key of idA), compute s' = n - s, v' = v^1 from the original signature and call idA.addClaim(1, 1, claimIssuer, (r, s', v'), KYC_DATA, \"\"). isClaimValid accepts it because the new bytes are not revoked. 3) token.transfer(a1, 1) (or any amount to a1) now passes isVerified and succeeds."}]}
